blogPosts.title: How to Prevent Blocked Drains in Your Eltham Home
blogPosts.excerpt: Practical tips to keep your drains clear in Eltham, avoiding common blockages caused by local factors.
body: Blocked drains are a frequent issue in Eltham homes, often due to tree roots, grease buildup, or foreign objects. Prevention is key to avoiding costly repairs and disruptions. At Sustain Plumbing, we advise Eltham residents on simple steps to maintain clear drains year-round.

First, be mindful of what goes down your kitchen sink. Avoid pouring oil, grease, or food scraps, as these solidify and cause blockages. Use drain screens to catch debris, and regularly flush drains with hot water. In Eltham, where cooking is a household staple, this habit can prevent many kitchen drain issues.

In bathrooms, hair and soap scum are common culprits. Install hair catchers in showers and baths, and clean them regularly. Eltham's hard water can exacerbate soap scum buildup, so consider using water softeners or regular vinegar flushes to dissolve deposits.

Outdoor drains in Eltham are vulnerable to leaves, dirt, and tree roots. Keep gutters and drains clear of debris, especially during autumn. Tree roots are a major concern in leafy suburbs like Eltham, as they seek moisture and can invade pipes. Regular inspections with CCTV cameras can detect early root intrusion.

Avoid flushing non-degradable items like wet wipes, sanitary products, or cotton balls, which cause severe blockages. Educate your household about proper disposal, and use bins for waste. In Eltham's family homes, this practice is crucial for drain health.

Schedule annual drain cleaning with Sustain Plumbing. Our high-pressure jetting services remove buildup and prevent blockages, tailored to Eltham's specific plumbing needs. We also offer pipe relining for damaged sections, ensuring long-term durability.

By following these tips, Eltham homeowners can minimise blocked drains and maintain efficient plumbing systems. Contact us for more advice or to book a drain inspection—keeping your home's plumbing in top shape is our priority.

blogPosts.title: Gas Safety Tips for Eltham Residents
blogPosts.excerpt: Essential gas safety advice for Eltham homes, covering appliance maintenance, leak detection, and compliance.
body: Gas safety is critical for Eltham households, where gas appliances are common for heating, cooking, and hot water. At Sustain Plumbing, we emphasize regular checks to prevent hazards and ensure compliance with Australian standards.

Start by inspecting your gas appliances annually. Look for signs of damage, such as yellow flames instead of blue, which indicate incomplete combustion and carbon monoxide risk. In Eltham, where winters are cold, gas heaters are widely used—schedule professional servicing to keep them efficient and safe.

Detecting gas leaks early is vital. Smell for a rotten egg odor, listen for hissing sounds near pipes or appliances, and check for dead vegetation around outdoor gas lines. Eltham's variable weather can affect gas infrastructure, so be vigilant after storms or temperature changes.

Ensure proper ventilation in areas with gas appliances. Blocked vents can lead to carbon monoxide buildup, which is odourless and deadly. Install carbon monoxide detectors in your Eltham home and test them regularly.

Never attempt DIY gas work. Always hire licensed gas fitters like Sustain Plumbing for installations, repairs, or modifications. In Eltham, DIY gas jobs can void insurance and violate safety regulations.

Know the emergency procedures. If you suspect a gas leak, turn off the supply at the meter, ventilate the area, and call us immediately. Avoid using electrical switches or open flames, which can ignite gas.
Educate your family about gas safety, including the location of shut-off valves and emergency contacts. In Eltham's community-focused suburbs, sharing this knowledge enhances neighborhood safety.
Regular maintenance by professionals ensures your gas system remains safe and efficient. Contact Sustain Plumbing for gas safety inspections in Eltham—we're here to protect your home and loved ones.
